The word "than" introduces the second part of the comparison, and "I" is the subject pronoun that complements the comparison. This construction adheres to the standard rule for formal English.
  • While "a better player than me" is commonly used in informal speech, particularly in everyday conversation, it is considered less formal than "a better player than I." In more formal or written contexts, it is preferable to use the nominative pronoun "I" after "than."

Therefore, for a more formal or grammatically correct expression, the sentence should read: "Farah may be a better player than I."
